newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada to raise some ex-Cda cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada to raise some ex-Cda cargo rates.

text.p: Air Canada will hike North Atlantic cargo rates three percent and add fuel surcharges on domestic and ex-North America freight to Europe which will come into effect on either December or January 1, an official said.
On December 1, it is introducing a US$0.10 per kilogram surcharge on shipments from the U.S. and Caribbean to Europe, India and Israel, matching action taken by major U.S. and foreign carriers.

From January 1, it will levy a surcharge of C$0.12/kg ex-Canada to Europe on all freight except horsemeat and lobster shipments, where the surcharge will be C$0.05/kg. At the same time, a domestic fuel surcharge of C$0.05/kg will take effect.
Also in January Air Canada will raise basic international cargo rates ex-Canada on all transatlantic corridors.
That increase, he said, is a first move to return to higher rate levels of a year ago. Air Canada and its competitors reduced Canada rates last April amid soft global market conditions, he said.
Air Canada imposed a C$0.12/kg on shipments from Europe to North America on November 15, which is holding, the official said.

It is waiting to raise ex-Canada rates until January 1 because of a September commitment to major Canadian-based customers not to raise export rates charges through December 31, the official said. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
